segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
unless permitted to proceed by another device

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal: 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...}; several states may be displayed at once'. A steady red with a green turn arrow is a head displaying circular_red (the steady red; flashing_red is a separate state) together with green_arrow(dir) for a turn direction dir ∈ {left, right, u_turn}, and not circular_green (that combination is the circular-green-with-arrow case of another paragraph).

'Pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ("a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device"), claimed by id and never expanded.

Facing, as the index maps 'facing such a signal' and 'pedestrians facing the signal': the head's dev.position ('location of the device head / sign face') lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the pedestrian's kin.position ('position of the body's reference point') and the pedestrian's kin.heading ('direction the body points') makes with the line to the head an angle whose cosine is at least p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos; the head's position is used for facing only, never as a stop line or crossing, so its 'not a stand-in for' clause does not apply. 'Such a signal' is the vehicular signal of NRS 484B.307, a head controlling a junction: it governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself') the intersection i (st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet') or a travel region g (st.travel_region, the kinds a device governs) that is an approach to i (st.lane_enters: 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'). The junction is the one across which the pedestrian faces the head, so its body lies within the same facing reach of i (st.region_geometry: 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'); a head faced within that reach controls a junction no farther away, so the bound ties the junction to the pedestrian and adds no limit the facing does not already set. The distance does not stand for the head belonging to the junction, which dev.governs and st.lane_enters state; dev.governs is not used as a position, st.lane_enters not for occupancy.

A pedestrian facing the signal stands on the highway already (DEF-NRS-484A-095: "the entire width between the boundary lines", which includes its sidewalks), so what it can enter is the vehicular part: its footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a st.roadway ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic') or a st.lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway'), having overlapped no roadway or lane and no st.median_or_divider ('dividing section between roadways') or st.safety_zone ('an area within the highway marked off for pedestrians') at the previous observation. A pedestrian stepping from a median or a safety zone is continuing a crossing already begun within the highway, not entering it. st.roadway's exclusion (not the sidewalk) is exactly why it is read; st.lane is not used as a lateral position.

The other device is a pedestrian signal head (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute when a timer is displayed'). By NRS 484B.283(1)(d)(1) and (2) a pedestrian facing such a head may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal while it shows walk, or while it flashes with a countdown timer: the subject is permitted to proceed where, at the judged observation, its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a roadway or lane q governed (dev.governs) by a pedestrian head d that it faces (dev.position, kin.position, kin.heading with p.ped_signal_facing_cos and p.ped_signal_facing_reach, as the accepted 283 nodes read facing and 'in the direction of the signal') and d shows walk, or dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute. The pedestrian-signal rules of NRS 484B.283 that engage for the subject are composed on s6 as exceptions besides.

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian). At the judged observation there are a traffic signal head h (dev.traffic_signal) displaying circular_red together with green_arrow(dir) for some dir in {left, right, u_turn} and not displaying circular_green, and an intersection i (st.intersection) such that h governs i (dev.governs(h, i)) or h governs a travel region g (dev.governs(h, g), g of kind st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters(g, i); the subject's body lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of i (st_region_geometry_distance(subject, i) at or below it); and the subject faces h: with Δ the vector from the subject's kin.position to h's dev.position and u the subject's kin.heading, u·Δ > 0, (u·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach². Excepted (permitted to proceed by another device, span s5): at the judged observation the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a region q of kind st.roadway or st.lane governed (dev.governs(d, q)) by a pedestrian signal head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) that shows walk, or dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute, and that the subject faces: with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and u its kin.heading, u·Δ > 0, (u·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Excepted also (span s6) where NRS_484B_283_1d1, NRS_484B_283_1d2, NRS_484B_283_1d3_o1 or NRS_484B_283_1d4_o1 is engaged for the subject (ruleApplies, subject mapped to subject): where a pedestrian-signal rule of NRS 484B.283 governs the subject's crossing, that rule decides.
obligation: The subject does not enter the roadway at the judged observation: it is not the case that its footprint overlaps some region of kind st.roadway or st.lane (rel.occupies) here while the condition 'its footprint overlaps some roadway or lane, or some st.median_or_divider or st.safety_zone' holds here and did not hold at the previous observation (rises of that condition). A pedestrian on the sidewalk is compliant; one stepping from the sidewalk or any place off the roadway onto a roadway or lane is violated; one continuing from a median or a safety zone does not enter. Where the previous observation is missing or the occupancy it needs is unobserved, unknown.

narrowings.why: A pedestrian facing the signal already stands on the highway (its sidewalk, within the boundary lines DEF-NRS-484A-095 names), so entering the highway is read as stepping onto its vehicular part, a roadway or lane, from a place that is neither a roadway or lane nor a median or safety zone; this is the reading the accepted NRS 484B.283(1)(d)(3) and (4) nodes give 'entered the highway' (a step from a sidewalk onto a roadway or lane).

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian stands on the corner sidewalk next to intersection i. Head h, across i, governs a lane g that enters i and displays circular_red with green_arrow(left), no circular_green; the pedestrian faces h within reach and within the facing angle. No pedestrian signal is present and no other road user. The pedestrian steps off the sidewalk: its footprint comes to overlap a roadway, having overlapped no roadway, lane, median or safety zone at the previous observation.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the pedestrian stays on the sidewalk while h displays the red with the arrow.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but h displays circular_green alone; the pedestrian steps into the roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the head's position is not observed (dev.position absent), so whether the pedestrian faces h is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a pedestrian signal head d governs the roadway the pedestrian steps onto, faces the pedestrian across the crossing within reach and angle, and shows walk.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in branch_1, but d shows dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As in branch_1, but d shows dont_walk_steady: NRS_484B_283_1d4_o1 is engaged for the subject (it steps onto a roadway d governs, facing d, not having overlapped it before), so that rule, not this one, judges the step.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but at the previous observation the pedestrian stood on a median between two roadways (and on no roadway or lane); it steps onto the second roadway: a continuing crossing, no entry.
